title: One-page oddities docket — quick eval notes
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick capture of weird outputs and tiny local rubrics I used while poking at the 7B quantized variant this morning. Not formal — meant to be a single-pager for later triage or to drop into a bug report.

Environment:
- model: open-7b-q4_0 (local dev image)
- quant: q4_0
- runtime: container-local (cpu+small-gpu), batch=1, max_tokens=120
- prompt template: small-context-instruct-v2 (see confluence:EVAL-playbook-72)

Ad-hoc micro-rubric (3 quick axes, score 0–3):
- Accuracy: does the output contain factual errors or hallucinated claims? (0 none, 3 lots)
- Instruction-following: respects role, format and step instructions? (0 good, 3 broken)
- Verbosity/format: adheres to requested length/structure? (0 good, 3 too long/malformed)

Representative samples and notes:
1) Sample A — prompt: "Summarize this policy in two bullets:" (small paragraph about data retention)
   output: 4 short sentences, first two fine, then a long paragraph that repeats detail and adds a speculative claim about retention periods being enforced by legal rather than engineering.
   scores: Accuracy=2, Instr-following=2, Verbosity=2
   quick thought: prefix cache hit? maybe KV reuse from previous test where legal context present. Try cold-start/invalidate cache.

2) Sample B — prompt: "Create a code snippet: Python function to normalize whitespace"
   output: returns a function but uses deprecated re.sub flags and a non-imported module alias (re2).
   scores: Accuracy=3, Instr-following=1, Verbosity=0
   thought: model sometimes invents library names under low-temp; ensure sampling/top-p settings safe (I was using top_p=0.95). Lowering sampling produces more conservative but stilted code.

3) Sample C — multi-step instruction, asked for 3-step checklist; output produces 4 steps and final step is an irrelevant troubleshooting item.
   scores: Accuracy=1, Instr-following=3, Verbosity=2
   note: instruction-following worst when prompt contains an inline example in bullet style. Might need stronger chain-of-thought guard rails or explicit "only produce N items" pattern.

Quick regression observations (compared to baseline run from 2025-01-25):
- Latency: median +12% token-latency on q4_0 under small-gpu due to a different kernel selection (observed spike at warm-up tokens). Follow-up: capture perf trace (obs/trace-0218) and compare to baseline trace id 0125.
- Accuracy drift: small uptick in hallucinations for short factual tasks. Hypothesis: quantization combined with top_p>0.9 amplifies creative errors. Test: run same prompts under top_p=0.7, q8_0 and non-quantized.
- Instruction following: roughly same, but degraded on list-length enforcement. Possibly a prompt-formatter change in template pipeline (check recent PR: github:pr/rl-eval-harness/58).

Immediate actions (to do, short):
- [ ] Re-run Sample A/B/C with cold process (restart container) to rule out cache bleed.
- [ ] Re-run with top_p=0.7 and temperature=0.0 on 10 seeds, record divergence.
- [ ] Add a tiny guard in the prompt: "strictly return two bullets, no additional commentary" and see effect.
- [ ] Upload perf trace to obs (link to trace id) and tag infra for kernel selection check.

Hypotheses to triage (for next deep-dive):
- Kernel selection: new kernel fallback path for attention at seq_len=64 causes occasional re-gen of attention buffers — triggers latency spikes and subtle token inconsistency.
- Context bleed: local test harness doesn't clear ephemeral prompt examples between runs; KV cache TTL config might be mis-set during dev runs.
- Sampling/quantization interaction: higher top_p exposes quantized model to lower-prob token tails that the quantized representation misestimates.

Notes-to-self / heuristics discovered:
- When encountering invented library names in code outputs, toggle temp->0.0 and top_p->0.5 for a quick repro. If still present, mark as hallucination class: "invented-apis".
- For list-length issues, an explicit suffix token like "<END-LIST>" in the prompt often forces termination in this model. Use sparingly in customer-facing prompts.

Scratch log (commands I ran):
- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/outputs -d "{\"model\":\"open-7b-q4_0\",\"input\":\"Summarize...\"}" --header 'Content-Type: application/json'
- docker restart eval-runner-dev && sleep 6 && run-local-trace --out trace-0218.json

Wrap-up: this is a capture only — good candidates for formal tickets: (1) investigate kernel-selection perf trace, (2) add prompt-formatter QA to pipeline, (3) small A/B on sampling+quant configs. Drop this into the weekly triage if no one else picks it up.

— z
